lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: Grammar: Agreement, Pronouns, Tenses and Voice

lines: A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb. Find the true subject first: phrases such as "of the students" or "along with his friends" do not change it.

Words such as each, every, everyone, either and neither are singular. With "either ... or" and "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. A collective noun (team, jury, class) acting as one unit is singular.
One of the teachers ___ (is / are) absent today.
The subject is "one", not "teachers". "Of the teachers" is only a phrase describing it.
Pronouns change form by their job. Subject forms: I, he, she, we, they, who. Object forms: me, him, her, us, them, whom. After a preposition (to, for, between, with), use the object form.
Test "who" or "whom" by answering the question yourself: if the answer is "him", use whom; if it is "he", use who.
The principal gave the award to ___ (she and I / her and me).
"To" is a preposition, so both pronouns take the object form. Check by removing one: "gave it to me", not "to I".
Perfect tenses show completion before a point in time: has/have + past participle (present perfect), had + past participle (past perfect), will have + past participle (future perfect).

In the active voice the subject does the action ("The class planted trees"). In the passive voice the subject receives it ("Trees were planted by the class"). Prefer the active voice unless the doer is unknown or unimportant.
Cover the words between the subject and the verb with your finger. The sentence that remains shows which verb fits.
Saying "between you and I". "Between" is a preposition, so the correct form is "between you and me".
Parallel structure means items in a list or comparison have the same grammatical form: "to read, to write and to speak" or "reading, writing and speaking", not a mix.

A modifier should sit next to the word it describes. A dangling modifier has nothing in the sentence to describe: "After finishing the test, the bell rang" (the bell did not finish the test). The position of "only" changes the meaning: "Only Ana passed" (no one else did) is not "Ana only passed" (she merely passed). Lay (laid, laid) takes an object: lay the books down. Lie (lay, lain) does not: lie down. The past tense of "lie" is "lay".
Fix: "After finishing the test, the bell rang."
Make the person who finished the test the subject of the main clause.
sections.answer: After finishing the test, I heard the bell ring.

lines: A run-on sentence joins two complete sentences with no punctuation. A comma splice joins them with only a comma. Fix either with a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus a conjunction (and, but, so).
Some prepositions come in fixed pairs: good at, interested in, afraid of, depend on, different from.
Choose the correct word: "___ (Its / It's) going to rain this afternoon."
The sentence means "It is going to rain", so use the contraction "it's". "Its" shows possession, as in "the dog wagged its tail".

Commonly confused words: affect (verb, to influence) and effect (noun, a result); than (comparison) and then (time); their (possession), there (place) and they're (they are); principal (head of a school, or main) and principle (a rule or belief).

Spelling: double the final consonant before -ing or -ed in short words with one vowel and one final consonant (stop, stopping). Words such as accommodate, committee and occurrence have double letters worth memorizing.
Mixing forms in a list, such as "She likes dancing, to sing and swims". Choose one form for all items.
A synonym has the same or nearly the same meaning; an antonym has the opposite meaning. Read the instruction carefully: "closest in meaning" asks for a synonym.
In vocabulary-in-context items, the sentence gives clues: a definition, an example, a contrast ("but", "unlike") or a cause.
The instructions were so obscure that no one knew what to do. What does "obscure" mean?
The clue "no one knew what to do" shows the instructions were unclear.

Common figures of speech: simile (comparison using like or as), metaphor (direct comparison), personification (human qualities given to things), hyperbole (exaggeration), irony (the opposite of what is expected) and onomatopoeia (words that imitate sounds).
An idiom means something different from its words: "hit the books" means to study hard; "a piece of cake" means very easy.
What figure of speech is in "The wind whispered through the trees"?
Whispering is a human action given to the wind.
An analogy compares two relationships. First state the relationship of the given pair in a sentence ("A pen is a tool a writer uses"), then find the pair with the same relationship.
For analogies, make the relationship sentence specific. "Related to" is too vague; "is a tool used by", "is a part of" and "is the opposite of" lead to one answer.
Choosing a word that is only related to the given word. "Sleepy" is related to "lethargic" but does not mean the same as "sluggish and without energy".

The communication process: a sender encodes a message, sends it through a channel, and a receiver decodes it and gives feedback. Noise is anything that disrupts the message, such as a loud room or unclear wording.
Register is the level of formality. Formal writing (letters, reports) avoids slang, contractions and text abbreviations; it is clear, polite and complete.
Speeches by purpose: informative (to explain), persuasive (to convince), entertaining (to amuse) and special-occasion speeches (to honor or welcome).
In reading, the topic sentence states the main idea of a paragraph; the other sentences support it. The tone is the writer's attitude toward the subject.
"Two students from that school were rude to me, so all students there are rude." What fallacy is this?
The conclusion about everyone is drawn from too few examples.

Common fallacies: ad hominem (attacking the person), bandwagon (everyone believes it), hasty generalization (too few examples), false dilemma (only two choices when there are more), and straw man (twisting an argument to attack it easily). In a syllogism, "All A are B; some B are C" proves nothing about A and C, because the middle term is never fully linked to both (undistributed middle). To weaken a cause-and-effect claim, look for another factor that could explain the result (a confounding factor). Appeal to common practice treats what people usually do as what is right.
In academic writing, a summary states the main ideas briefly; a paraphrase restates an idea in your own words; a quotation copies the exact words. All three need a citation.
In intercultural communication, avoid stereotypes, ask instead of assume, and be careful with humor and gestures, which can mean different things in other cultures.
Thinking that changing a few words in a source avoids plagiarism. A paraphrase or summary still needs a citation.

lessons.subject: Filipino
lessons.title: Gramatika: Mga Bahagi ng Pananalita at Pangungusap

lines: Pangngalan ang ngalan ng tao, bagay, lugar o pangyayari. Pantangi ito kung tiyak (Maynila, Jose) at pambalana kung pangkalahatan (lungsod, bata). Ang panghalip ay pumapalit sa pangngalan (siya, kami).

Ang pandiwa ay salitang kilos. Ang pang-uri ay naglalarawan sa pangngalan o panghalip; ang pang-abay ay naglalarawan sa pandiwa, pang-uri o kapwa pang-abay. Uri ng pang-abay: pamaraan (paano), pamanahon (kailan), panlunan (saan), pang-agam (di-katiyakan: marahil, siguro, baka) at panang-ayon (oo, talaga). Pokus ng pandiwa: kung ang paksa ang gumawa, pokus sa tagaganap ("Bumili si Ana ng aklat"); kung ang paksa ang bagay na ginawan, pokus sa layon ("Binili ni Ana ang aklat").

Aspekto ng pandiwa: perpektibo (tapos na: kumain), imperpektibo (ginagawa pa: kumakain), kontemplatibo (gagawin pa lamang: kakain). May ikaapat na madalas itanong: katatapos o perpektibong katatapos (kagagawa lamang: kakakain, kaaalis), na binubuo ng ka- at inuulit na unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
Ang pang-angkop (na, -ng, -g) ay nag-uugnay sa panuring at salitang tinuturingan: batang masipag, puting damit. Ang pangatnig (at, ngunit, kaya) ay nag-uugnay ng mga salita o sugnay.
Punan ang patlang: "Umalis siya ___ maaga."
Ang "nang" ay ginagamit bago ang pang-abay na pamaraan o pamanahon na naglalarawan sa pandiwa. Ang "ng" ay ginagamit bago ang pangngalan: "kumain ng saging".
Ang salitang-ugat ay ang salitang walang panlapi: sa "kinagigiliwan", ang ugat ay "giliw".

Uri ng pangungusap ayon sa gamit: pasalaysay (nagkukuwento, nagtatapos sa tuldok), patanong (?), pautos o pakiusap, at padamdam (!). Ayon sa kayarian: payak (isang sugnay na makapag-iisa), tambalan (dalawa o higit pang sugnay na makapag-iisa), hugnayan (isang sugnay na makapag-iisa at isang di-makapag-iisa, gaya ng may "dahil" o "kung") at langkapan (dalawa o higit pang makapag-iisa at isa o higit pang di-makapag-iisa).
Para sa "ng" at "nang": kung masasagot ng "paano" o "kailan" ang salitang kasunod, karaniwang "nang" ang wasto.
Paggamit ng "kay" para sa lugar. Ang "kay" ay para sa ngalan ng tao (kay Ana); ang "sa" ay para sa lugar (sa palengke).
Ang kasingkahulugan ay salitang may parehong kahulugan (masaya, maligaya); ang kasalungat ay salitang may kabaligtarang kahulugan (masaya, malungkot).
Ang idyoma ay pahayag na hindi tuwiran ang kahulugan: "bukas-palad" (mapagbigay), "kapit-tuko" (ayaw bumitaw), "nagbibilang ng poste" (walang trabaho).
Ano ang kahulugan ng idyomang "bukas-palad"?
Ang taong bukas-palad ay laging handang tumulong at magbigay.

Mga tayutay: pagtutulad (paghahambing gamit ang "tulad ng", "parang"), pagwawangis (tuwirang paghahambing), pagsasatao (pagbibigay-katangiang pantao sa bagay), pagmamalabis (eksaherasyon) at onomatopeya (paggaya sa tunog). Sa pagtawag, kinakausap ang bagay na wala o hindi buhay na para bang naroroon ("O kalayaan, kailan ka darating?").
Antas ng wika: pambansa at pampanitikan (pormal); lalawiganin, kolokyal at balbal (impormal). Halimbawa ng balbal: "lodi", "erpat".
Anong tayutay ang "Umiiyak ang langit"?
Ang pag-iyak ay kilos ng tao na ibinigay sa langit.
Sa pagbaybay ng hiram na salita, sundin ang bigkas: "silya" (silla), "telebisyon", "kompyuter". Panatilihin ang orihinal na baybay ng mga pangngalang pantangi at teknikal na termino.
Pagkalito sa pagtutulad at pagwawangis. Kung may "tulad ng", "parang" o "kawangis", pagtutulad iyon; kung wala, pagwawangis.
Ayon sa Artikulo XIV, Seksyon 6 ng Saligang Batas ng 1987, Filipino ang wikang pambansa. Ang Filipino at Ingles ang mga wikang opisyal para sa komunikasyon at pagtuturo.
Apat na paraan ng pagpapahayag: pagsasalaysay (nagkukuwento), paglalarawan (naglalarawan), paglalahad (nagpapaliwanag) at pangangatwiran (nanghihikayat gamit ang katwiran).

Mga uri ng teksto: impormatibo (nagbibigay ng impormasyon), deskriptibo (naglalarawan), naratibo (nagsasalaysay), persweysib (nanghihikayat), prosidyural (nagtuturo ng hakbang) at argumentatibo (naglalahad ng posisyon na may ebidensya).
Ang sanaysay ay may panimula (pumupukaw ng interes at naglalahad ng paksa), katawan (nagpapaliwanag) at wakas (nagbubuod o nag-iiwan ng kaisipan).
Anong uri ng teksto ang "Mga Hakbang sa Pagluluto ng Sinigang"?
Nagtuturo ito ng sunud-sunod na hakbang para makagawa ng isang bagay.

Panitikan: ang tuluyan o prosa ay nasusulat sa karaniwang pangungusap (maikling kuwento, nobela, sanaysay, alamat, pabula, kuwentong-bayan); ang patula ay may sukat at tugma (tula, awit, korido, epiko). Ang dula ay itinatanghal sa entablado.
Mahahalagang akda: ang Noli Me Tangere (1887) at El Filibusterismo (1891) ni José Rizal; ang Florante at Laura ni Francisco Balagtas, isang awit; at ang Ibong Adarna, isang korido.
Sa akademikong pagsulat, ang abstrak ay maikling buod ng pananaliksik; ang bibliograpiya ay listahan ng mga sanggunian. Pormal ang wika at may batayan ang mga pahayag.
Para matukoy ang uri ng teksto, itanong: "Ano ang layunin ng manunulat?" Ang layunin ang nagtatakda ng uri.
Pag-aakalang Tagalog ang wikang pambansa. Ayon sa Saligang Batas ng 1987, ito ay Filipino, na pinayayaman ng iba't ibang wika sa bansa.

lessons.subject: Science and Technology
lessons.title: Living Things: Cells, Plants and the Human Body

lines: The cell is the basic unit of life. The nucleus holds most of the genetic material (DNA), mitochondria release energy through cellular respiration, and ribosomes make proteins. Plant cells also have chloroplasts and a cell wall.

A gene is a segment of DNA that carries instructions for a trait and is passed from parents to offspring. A dominant allele (T) hides a recessive one (t). Crossing two Tt parents gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3/4 show the dominant trait, and 2/3 of those are Tt.
In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, releasing oxygen. Roots absorb water and minerals; leaves make food; the stem carries materials between them.

Living things are grouped into kingdoms, such as plants, animals and fungi. Fungi, such as mushrooms and molds, absorb nutrients instead of making their own food. Mammals breathe with lungs, have hair and nurse their young with milk, so whales and bats are mammals while sharks are fish and penguins are birds. In a food chain, only about 10% of the energy passes to the next level.
Which gas do plants release as a product of photosynthesis?
Carbon dioxide and water go in; glucose and oxygen come out.

Body systems work together. The heart pumps blood through arteries (away from the heart) and veins (back to the heart). The pancreas makes insulin, which controls blood sugar. The skin is the largest organ.
Vaccines train the immune system to recognize a germ, so the body can fight the real infection quickly. Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D.
Remember "A for Away": arteries carry blood away from the heart.
Thinking only plant cells have mitochondria. Both plant and animal cells have them; only plant cells have chloroplasts.

Matter is made of atoms, the smallest units of an element. Water boils at 100°C and freezes at 0°C at sea level. On the pH scale, 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic. The scale is logarithmic: each step of 1 is a tenfold change, so pH 3 is 100 times more acidic than pH 5. An object floats if its density is less than water's, and the fraction under water equals its density ÷ water's density (0.75 g/cm³ floats three-quarters submerged).
Energy takes many forms: chemical (in food and fuels), kinetic (motion), potential (position), thermal, electrical, light and sound. Energy changes form but is not created or destroyed.

Newton's laws: (1) an object stays at rest or in motion unless a net force acts on it (inertia); (2) F = ma; (3) every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Gravity pulls objects toward Earth's center; friction opposes motion. A ball thrown up still accelerates downward at about 9.8 m/s² at its highest point, where its velocity is momentarily zero. Bulbs in parallel each get the full voltage and work independently; bulbs in series share the voltage, and one broken bulb stops them all.
Electric current is measured in amperes, voltage in volts, and resistance in ohms.
A net force of 12 N acts on a 4 kg cart. What is its acceleration?

Renewable energy sources are naturally replenished: solar, wind, hydro and geothermal (the Philippines is a major geothermal producer). Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas are non-renewable.
Sound is a wave that needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas); it cannot travel through a vacuum.
For F = ma problems, write down what you know (F, m or a) before choosing which form to use: a = F/m, m = F/a.
Confusing mass and weight. Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the force of gravity on it (newtons).
The atmosphere has layers: the troposphere (where weather happens), the stratosphere (with the ozone layer that absorbs ultraviolet rays), the mesosphere and the thermosphere.
The water cycle: evaporation (liquid to vapor), condensation (vapor to droplets, forming clouds), precipitation (rain) and collection in bodies of water.

The solar system: the Sun, a star, is at the center, orbited by eight planets in this order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. The four inner planets are small and rocky; the four outer planets are giants made mostly of gas and ice.
Mars is the "Red Planet" because of iron oxide (rust) in its soil. Jupiter is the largest planet; Venus is the hottest. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Which stage of the water cycle returns water from clouds to the ground?
Rain, snow and hail are forms of precipitation.
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat and drives climate change. Effects include stronger typhoons, sea-level rise and changing rainfall.
In the Philippines, PHIVOLCS monitors volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis; PAGASA monitors weather and typhoons. A seismograph records earthquakes.

Science and technology shape society: early-warning systems and emergency alerts save lives during disasters, while new technologies also raise ethical questions about privacy, health and the environment.
Link agencies to hazards: PHIVOLCS for things from the ground (quakes, volcanoes), PAGASA for things from the sky (weather, typhoons).
Planet order: "My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Nachos" (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune).
Mixing up the greenhouse effect and the ozone hole. The ozone layer blocks ultraviolet rays; greenhouse gases trap heat. They are related to different problems.
Order of operations: parentheses, exponents, multiplication and division (left to right), then addition and subtraction (left to right), often remembered as PEMDAS.
To add fractions, use a common denominator: 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12. Never add the denominators.
Simplify: 5 + 4 × 3
Multiply first: 4 × 3 = 12. Then add: 5 + 12 = 17. Working left to right (9 × 3 = 27) is a common mistake.
Percent means "per hundred". To find a percent of a number, change the percent to a decimal and multiply: 20% of 150 = 0.20 × 150 = 30.

Percent increase or decrease = (change ÷ original) × 100. To compare fractions, decimals and percents, change them all to decimals. Successive percent changes multiply: a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease gives 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96, a 4% net decrease. A 40% markup followed by a 20% discount gives 1.40 × 0.80 = 1.12, a 12% profit on cost.
A bag costs ₱400 after a 20% discount. What was the original price?
The sale price is 80% of the original: 0.80 × P = 400, so P = ₱500.
A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ...). 2 is the only even prime; 1 is not prime.
For number patterns, check the difference between terms (adding), the ratio (multiplying), or special sequences such as squares (1, 4, 9, 16) and Fibonacci (1, 1, 2, 3, 5).
To round, look only at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less stays.
Finding the original price by adding the discount to the sale price. A 20% discount is 20% of the original, not of the sale price.

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Ratio, Rate and Everyday Word Problems

lines: A ratio compares quantities. If boys and girls are in the ratio 2 : 3 in a class of 30, there are 5 parts of 6 learners each: 12 boys and 18 girls.

Rate = amount per unit: speed = distance ÷ time; unit price = total cost ÷ number of items. A map scale of 1 cm : 2 km means each centimeter stands for 2 km. Objects moving apart in opposite directions separate at the sum of their speeds; in the same direction, at the difference.
Elapsed time: count to the next full hour, then add the rest. From 8:40 a.m. to 11:10 a.m. is 20 minutes + 2 hours + 10 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes.
Four workers finish a job in 9 days. How long would six workers take at the same rate?
The job takes 4 × 9 = 36 worker-days. Six workers need 36 ÷ 6 = 6 days. More workers means fewer days.
Simple interest: I = P × r × t, with t in years. ₱2,000 at 5% for 3 years earns 2,000 × 0.05 × 3 = ₱300.
Average (mean) = sum ÷ number of values, so sum = average × number of values.
A die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
The favorable outcomes are 5 and 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.

Probability = favorable outcomes ÷ total possible outcomes, a value from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Without replacement, the second draw has one fewer item: two reds from 4 red and 6 blue is 4/10 × 3/9.
To solve an equation, undo operations in reverse order on both sides: 2x + 5 = 17, so 2x = 12 and x = 6.
In word problems, write what is asked before computing. Many wrong answers are correct numbers for a different question, such as the number of boys instead of girls.
Using months as the time in I = Prt. Change months to years first: 6 months = 0.5 year.
Metric conversions: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 L = 1,000 mL. To change to a smaller unit, multiply; to a larger unit, divide.
Perimeter is the distance around a figure. Rectangle: P = 2(l + w). Square: P = 4s. Circle (circumference): C = 2πr.

Area is the space inside a figure, in square units. Rectangle: A = lw. Square: A = s². Triangle: A = ½bh. Circle: A = πr². A square's area is also diagonal² ÷ 2, useful when a square is drawn inside a circle (its diagonal is the diameter).
The angles of a triangle add up to 180°; the angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
A square has a perimeter of 32 cm. What is its area?
Each side is 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm, so the area is 8 × 8 = 64 cm².
Two angles of a triangle are 75° and 65°. What is the third angle?
Always check units: perimeter is in cm, m or km; area is in cm², m² or km². A unit mismatch often signals a wrong formula.
Mixing up perimeter and area, for example multiplying the sides of a rectangle when the question asks for the distance around it.

lessons.subject: Philippine History
lessons.title: Pre-colonial Society and the Spanish Period

lines: Before colonization, people lived in barangays led by a datu, traded with China and Southeast Asia, used scripts such as baybayin, and sailed in balangay boats. The Laguna Copperplate Inscription (about 900 CE) is the oldest known written document found in the country. Tagalog society had the maharlika (nobles), timawa (freemen) and alipin: the aliping namamahay had their own houses and property, while the aliping saguiguilid lived in the master's house and could be sold.

Historians use primary sources (made at the time, often by witnesses, such as Pigafetta's account of Magellan's voyage) and secondary sources (later interpretations, such as textbooks). Readings in Philippine History stresses checking both. External criticism tests whether a source is authentic (its material, date and author); internal criticism tests whether its content is credible. When accounts conflict, historians weigh each author's position and purpose and check them against other sources (corroboration). An anachronism, a detail the supposed author could not have known, is a sign that a source may not be authentic.
Magellan reached the islands in 1521 and was killed at Mactan by Lapulapu's forces. Legazpi founded the first permanent Spanish settlement in Cebu in 1565 and made Manila the capital in 1571.

Colonial systems: encomienda (land and people entrusted to Spaniards to collect tribute), tributo (tax), polo y servicio (forced labor), reducción (moving people into church-centered towns) and the galleon trade linking Manila and Acapulco (1565–1815).
Which revolt against Spain lasted the longest?
Francisco Dagohoy's revolt in Bohol lasted about 85 years (1744–1829). Other revolts include those of Diego and Gabriela Silang in Ilocos.
The first Filipino saint, Lorenzo Ruiz, was martyred in Japan in 1637 and canonized in 1987; Pedro Calungsod became the second in 2012.
Keep a short timeline: 1521 Magellan, 1565 Cebu, 1571 Manila, 1872 GOMBURZA, 1896 Revolution, 1898 independence proclaimed.
Treating a modern textbook as a primary source. A source is primary only if it comes from the time of the event.

lessons.subject: Philippine History
lessons.title: Reform, Revolution and the First Republic

lines: The execution of the priests Gomez, Burgos and Zamora (GOMBURZA) in 1872 stirred Filipino nationalism. In Spain, the Propaganda Movement of Rizal, Marcelo H. del Pilar and Graciano Lopez Jaena sought peaceful reforms through the newspaper La Solidaridad.

When reform failed, Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan on July 7, 1892. Emilio Jacinto, author of the Kartilya, was its "Brains". The Revolution began with the Cry of Pugad Lawin in August 1896. Historians debate the exact site and date (Pugad Lawin or Balintawak; August 23 or 26); the government officially marks it as August 23, 1896, at Pugad Lawin. The opening of the Suez Canal (1869) had shortened travel to Europe, helping ilustrados study abroad and liberal ideas spread. After the Cry came the Pact of Biak-na-Bato (December 1897), the Declaration of Independence at Kawit (June 12, 1898) and the Malolos Constitution (January 1899).

At the Tejeros Convention (1897), Emilio Aguinaldo was elected President. Independence was proclaimed in Kawit, Cavite, on June 12, 1898. Apolinario Mabini, the "Sublime Paralytic", was Aguinaldo's chief adviser and the "Brains of the Revolution".
The Malolos Constitution, drafted mainly by Felipe Calderón, set up the First Philippine Republic, inaugurated on January 23, 1899.
Who sewed the first Philippine flag in Hong Kong?
She sewed it with her daughter Lorenza and Delfina Herbosa de Natividad. Julián Felipe composed the music of the national anthem.

During the Spanish-American War, the U.S. fleet under Dewey defeated the Spanish fleet in Manila Bay (May 1, 1898). By the Treaty of Paris (December 10, 1898), Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States for $20 million.
Separate the two "Brains": Emilio Jacinto was the Brains of the Katipunan; Apolinario Mabini was the Brains of the Revolution.
Thinking independence was proclaimed in Malolos. It was proclaimed in Kawit; Malolos was where the Republic and its constitution were established.

lessons.subject: Philippine History
lessons.title: From the American Period to the Present

lines: The Philippine–American War began on February 4, 1899. The Americans set up a public school system (Act No. 74, 1901) taught by the Thomasites and used English as the medium of instruction.

The Tydings–McDuffie Act (1934) provided a ten-year transition. The Commonwealth was inaugurated on November 15, 1935, with Manuel L. Quezon as President. Under Governor-General Harrison (1913–1921), Filipinization put Filipinos in most civil service posts. The Philippine-American War began in February 1899 after Spain ceded the islands to the United States in the Treaty of Paris (December 1898) and the US refused to recognize the First Republic.
Japan invaded in December 1941. After Bataan fell on April 9, 1942, prisoners were forced on the Bataan Death March. The country was liberated in 1945.

Independence from the United States came on July 4, 1946, with Manuel Roxas as first President of the Third Republic. The 1947 parity amendment, tied to postwar aid and the Bell Trade Act, gave Americans equal rights with Filipinos to natural resources and public utilities, which nationalists opposed.
In what year did Ferdinand Marcos declare martial law through Proclamation No. 1081?

Proclamation No. 1081 is dated September 21, 1972, and Marcos announced it on September 23, 1972. Martial law was formally lifted on January 17, 1981 (Proclamation No. 2045), but Marcos kept the power to issue decrees (under Amendment No. 6 of 1976) and to detain people without trial until he was ousted in 1986.

The People Power Revolution along EDSA in February 1986, set off when Juan Ponce Enrile and Fidel Ramos broke away from Marcos after the disputed snap election, ended the Marcos regime; Corazon Aquino became President. The present Constitution was ratified on February 2, 1987; it limits martial law to 60 days and lets Congress revoke it and the Supreme Court review its basis.
Remember the two independence dates: June 12, 1898 (from Spain, now Independence Day) and July 4, 1946 (from the United States).
Mixing up the Commonwealth (1935, a transition under U.S. rule) with full independence (1946).

lessons.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
lessons.title: Rizal's Life: Family, Education, Exile and Death

lines: José Rizal was born on June 19, 1861, in Calamba, Laguna, to Francisco Mercado and Teodora Alonso. His mother's unjust imprisonment deeply affected him.

He earned a Bachelor of Arts with the highest grades (sobresaliente) at the Ateneo Municipal (1877), studied medicine at UST, finished his licentiate in medicine in Madrid, and trained in ophthalmology in Paris and Heidelberg, partly to treat his mother's eyes.
After founding La Liga Filipina in 1892, he was exiled to Dapitan (1892–1896), where he ran a school, practiced medicine and did community projects; Josephine Bracken lived with him there.

He volunteered as a doctor in Cuba but was arrested on the way and tried by a Spanish military court for rebellion, sedition and illegal association; the court held that his writings and La Liga Filipina had inspired the Revolution, though he had refused to support it. He was executed at Bagumbayan (now Rizal Park) on December 30, 1896, a date now observed every year as Rizal Day.
Which law requires the teaching of Rizal's life and works, especially his two novels, in all schools?
The Rizal Law (1956) was sponsored by Senators Claro M. Recto and Jose P. Laurel. December 30 is observed as Rizal Day.
Places in order: Calamba (birth), Ateneo and UST (studies), Madrid (medicine), Berlin and Ghent (novels), Dapitan (exile), Fort Santiago (prison), Bagumbayan (execution).
Thinking Rizal was executed at Fort Santiago. He was imprisoned there but executed at Bagumbayan.
Noli Me Tangere (Berlin, 1887, printed with Maximo Viola's help) exposed abuses of colonial society through Crisóstomo Ibarra, Maria Clara, Elias, Sisa and Padre Dámaso.
El Filibusterismo (Ghent, 1891, with Valentin Ventura's help) is dedicated to GOMBURZA. Ibarra returns as Simoun, a rich jeweler bent on revolution.

Essays: "The Indolence of the Filipino" blamed colonial conditions for so-called laziness; "The Philippines a Century Hence" warned Spain it would lose the colony without reforms. His annotation of Morga's Sucesos (1890) showed Filipinos had a rich pre-colonial culture.
In his 1889 letter to the young women of Malolos, he praised their wish to study and urged education and independent thinking.
Which pen name did Rizal use in La Solidaridad?
He also wrote as Dimasalang. Plaridel was Marcelo H. del Pilar's pen name.

La Liga Filipina (1892) was a civic group for unity and peaceful reform. "Mi Último Adiós", written before his execution, bids farewell to the country he loved and offers his life for it. At the end of El Filibusterismo, Simoun's uprising fails and Padre Florentino says freedom must be earned through virtue and sacrifice. In his December 1896 manifesto from prison, Rizal condemned the uprising and urged education first.
Link each novel to its helper: Noli with Viola, Fili with Ventura.
Confusing the dedications. The Noli is dedicated to the Philippines ("To My Country"); El Filibusterismo is dedicated to GOMBURZA.

Kant's deontology judges acts by duty and reason. His formula of universal law: act only on a rule you could will everyone to follow. His formula of humanity: never treat a person merely as a means, as when workers are used only as tools for profit. Consequences do not make an act right.

Utilitarianism (Bentham, Mill) judges acts by consequences: choose what brings the greatest good for the greatest number. Bentham measured pleasure and pain. Act utilitarianism judges each act by its results; rule utilitarianism follows the rules whose general practice brings the most good, such as keeping promises.

Aristotle's virtue ethics asks what a good person would do. Virtues are habits formed by practice and lie at the mean between extremes (courage between cowardice and rashness). The goal of life is eudaimonia, or flourishing.

Aquinas's natural law holds that reason can know basic moral rules from human nature, such as preserving life. Its principle of double effect allows an act with a good intended effect and a foreseen but unintended bad effect, such as strong pain relief that may shorten life.
A mayor builds a road that helps thousands, even though a few lose some farmland. Which theory most clearly supports this choice?
The decision rests on the overall balance of benefits over harms.

Other views: cultural relativism (morality depends on culture), ethical egoism (act in one's own interest), emotivism (moral statements express feelings), and social contract theory (Hobbes, Locke: people accept rules in exchange for order and protection). The Golden Rule asks us to treat others as we want to be treated.
Ask what each theory looks at: Kant looks at the rule and intention, utilitarians at the results, Aristotle at the character.
Thinking utilitarianism means doing whatever makes oneself happy. It counts the happiness of everyone affected; that is the difference from egoism.

lessons.subject: Ethics
lessons.title: Moral Agents, Dilemmas and Filipino Values

lines: Moral standards deal with serious matters that affect others' well-being; etiquette deals with manners. A moral dilemma is a choice where every option breaks some moral principle.

A person is morally responsible for an act done knowingly and freely. Conscience is reason's inner judgment of right and wrong in a particular situation; it should be formed by reflection and learning.
The common good is the set of social conditions that let everyone flourish. Human rights rest on the dignity of every person, as affirmed in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948).
Integrity applies in every setting: no bribery in public office, no cheating or plagiarism in school (academic integrity), and responsible stewardship of the environment for future generations.
A student reports a classmate's cheating even though friends will be upset. What virtue does this show?
Doing what is right despite the risk of rejection is moral courage.
Filipino values can help or hinder ethical choices: bayanihan and utang na loob build community, but pakikisama or hiya can lead people to go along with wrongdoing to avoid conflict.
In dilemma questions, identify the principles in conflict first (for example honesty versus loyalty), then judge which theory or value the answer applies.
Treating every disagreement as a moral issue. Choosing a paint color is a matter of taste; falsifying records is a moral issue.

Globalization is the growing interconnection of economies, cultures and peoples. Economic globalization includes trade, foreign direct investment and outsourcing, such as call centers serving foreign companies.

Free trade lowers barriers; protectionism raises them with tariffs to shield local industries. The WTO handles trade rules, the IMF monetary stability, and the World Bank development loans. By comparative advantage, each country gains by specializing in what it gives up the least to produce, even if another country is better at everything.

Cultural globalization spreads music, films and food worldwide. It can lead to homogenization (places looking alike) or glocalization (global products adapted to local tastes, such as rice meals at international fast-food chains). Marshall McLuhan called the media-linked world a "global village". Hybridization mixes foreign and local elements into something new, such as the jeepney made from American army jeeps.

The United Nations (1945) leads global governance; UNESCO handles education, science and culture. Non-state actors such as corporations and NGOs also shape world affairs. In the Security Council, a substantive resolution needs 9 of 15 votes and no "no" vote (veto) from the five permanent members: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Which regional organization did the Philippines help found in Bangkok in 1967?
The founders were Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. The ASEAN Economic Community aims at a single market but has no common currency.
International law also protects small states: in 2016 a tribunal under UNCLOS ruled in favor of the Philippines in its South China Sea case.
Match the organization to its job: WTO trade, IMF money, World Bank loans, UNESCO culture and heritage, WHO health.
Thinking globalization only spreads goods. It also spreads ideas, people, technologies and risks such as diseases.

lessons.subject: The Contemporary World
lessons.title: Global Issues: Migration, Inequality and Sustainability

lines: Overseas Filipino workers send remittances that support families and the economy; RA 8042 (amended by RA 10022) protects migrant workers, and RA 11641 created the Department of Migrant Workers. Brain drain is the loss of skilled professionals abroad. Urbanization is the movement of people from rural areas to cities.

Demography studies the size, makeup and change of populations through births, deaths and migration. The world population passed 8 billion in November 2022. Richer countries tend to have low birth rates and aging populations; many developing countries have young, fast-growing populations, which become a demographic dividend when enough jobs and schooling are available.
The Global South refers to developing countries, mostly in Africa, Asia and Latin America. The digital divide separates those with and without access to technology and the internet.

The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals target 2030; SDG 4 is quality education. The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep warming well below 2°C and to pursue 1.5°C. Under "common but differentiated responsibilities", all countries act on climate, but developed countries carry more because of their historical emissions and resources.
Shared problems such as climate change, pandemics, overfishing and human trafficking cross borders and need international cooperation.
A student joins a campaign against plastic pollution after learning how it affects oceans worldwide. Which idea does this show?
A global citizen is aware of belonging to a world community and acts responsibly toward it.
The Fourth Industrial Revolution (artificial intelligence, robotics, the internet of things) is changing work and daily life, bringing both opportunities and new divides.
For "which term" questions, focus on the key action: people leaving (emigration), skilled people leaving (brain drain), people moving to cities (urbanization).
Thinking the Global South simply means countries below the equator. The term is about economic and political position, not geography alone.

lessons.subject: Art Appreciation
lessons.title: Elements, Principles and Forms of Art

lines: Elements of art: line, shape, form, space, color, value (lightness or darkness) and texture (how a surface feels or seems to feel). Red, yellow and blue are the traditional primary colors. Linear perspective makes parallel lines meet at a vanishing point to show depth; atmospheric perspective makes distant things paler and less detailed.

Principles of design: balance (even visual weight), emphasis (a focal point), rhythm (repetition that creates movement), proportion, contrast and unity. The rule of thirds is a guide for composition. Balance can be symmetrical (mirrored), asymmetrical (different elements with equal visual weight) or radial (from a center). Complementary colors, opposite on the color wheel (blue and orange), create strong contrast; analogous colors sit next to each other. Hierarchical proportion makes figures larger to show importance, not size. Theories for judging art: imitationalism (realistic likeness), formalism (design), emotionalism (feeling) and instrumentalism (social purpose).

Forms: visual arts (painting, sculpture, architecture, photography) and performing arts (dance, music, theater). A mural is painted on a wall; a sculpture is three-dimensional. Art can serve personal, social and physical (useful) functions.

Movements: the Renaissance (Leonardo's Mona Lisa), Impressionism (light and everyday scenes), Pointillism (dots of color, Seurat), Cubism (geometric, many viewpoints, Picasso and Braque), Surrealism (dreamlike, Dalí) and abstract art (no recognizable subject). Expressionism distorts forms and colors to show inner feelings (Munch's The Scream).
A painter uses a bright red umbrella in an otherwise gray street scene so the viewer's eye goes there first. Which principle is used?
Emphasis creates a focal point, often through contrast of color or size.
Feldman's method of art criticism has four steps: description (what you see), analysis (how it is organized), interpretation (what it means) and judgment (its value).
Elements are the "ingredients" (line, color, texture); principles are the "recipe" for arranging them (balance, rhythm, emphasis).
Confusing value and hue. Hue is the color itself (blue); value is how light or dark it is (sky blue versus navy).

Painting: Juan Luna's Spoliarium won a gold medal in Madrid (1884), and Félix Resurrección Hidalgo won silver. Fernando Amorsolo, the first National Artist (1972), painted sunlit rural scenes. Carlos "Botong" Francisco painted murals of history and folklore.

Sculpture: Guillermo Tolentino made the UP Oblation and the Bonifacio Monument; Napoleon Abueva is the "Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture". Architecture: Leandro Locsin designed the Cultural Center of the Philippines. Additive sculpture builds up material (modeling clay); subtractive sculpture removes it (carving wood or stone). The bahay na bato combined a stone ground floor for strength with a wooden upper floor that flexed in earthquakes and wide capiz windows for air.

Music and dance: the kundiman is a traditional love song; Lucrecia Kasilag was a National Artist for Music; Francisca Reyes-Aquino documented folk dances; the Bayanihan company performs them worldwide.

Traditional arts: Maranao okir (curving, leaf-like designs), T'boli t'nalak (tie-dyed abaca cloth woven from dream patterns) and Ilocano inabel weaving. The Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Who sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan?
Tolentino also sculpted the Oblation, the symbol of the University of the Philippines.
Group National Artists by field: Amorsolo and Botong (visual arts), Tolentino and Abueva (sculpture), Locsin (architecture), Kasilag (music), Reyes-Aquino (dance).
Calling Juan Luna a National Artist. The Order of National Artists began in 1972, long after his death; he is honored as a master painter and patriot.

lessons.subject: Understanding the Self
lessons.title: Views of the Self: Philosophy, Psychology and Culture

lines: Philosophers: Socrates ("the unexamined life is not worth living"); Plato (soul of reason, spirit and appetite); Augustine (a soul seeking God); Descartes ("I think, therefore I am"); Locke (mind as a blank slate, tabula rasa); Hume (a bundle of perceptions); Merleau-Ponty (the embodied self).

Psychologists: William James (material, social and spiritual selves); Freud (id, ego, superego); Carl Rogers (real self versus ideal self; a large gap is incongruence); Carl Jung (the persona, our social mask). Freud's defense mechanisms include rationalization (giving an acceptable false reason), projection (seeing one's own feelings in others), denial and displacement (redirecting emotion to a safer target).

Sociology: George Herbert Mead held that the self develops through social interaction and taking the role of others. Festinger's social comparison theory says we judge ourselves by comparing with others. Cooley's looking-glass self forms from how we imagine others see and judge us. Comparing oneself with someone better off is upward comparison; with someone worse off, downward comparison.

East and the Philippines: Confucianism sees the self in relationships and duties; Buddhism teaches anattā, no permanent self. Virgilio Enriquez placed kapwa, a shared self with others, at the core of Filipino values; loob is the inner self.
Ana believes she is a good singer but a poor speller; overall she feels she is a worthwhile person. What is her overall sense of worth called?
Her beliefs about her traits are her self-concept; her overall valuing of herself is self-esteem.
Link each thinker to one phrase: Descartes "I think", Locke "blank slate", Hume "bundle", Rogers "real versus ideal".
Confusing self-concept and self-esteem. Self-concept is what you believe you are; self-esteem is how much you value yourself.

lessons.subject: Understanding the Self
lessons.title: Caring for the Self: Body, Mind, Spirit and Online Life

lines: The physical self needs sleep, exercise and good nutrition. Puberty's changes are driven by hormones. The spiritual self concerns beliefs, values and meaning, expressed in prayer, reflection and service.

The digital self is the identity we show online. A healthy digital self protects personal information, respects others and remembers that curated posts are not the whole person. The online disinhibition effect explains why people say things online that they would not say face to face.
Stress can be positive (eustress, which motivates) or harmful (distress, which overwhelms). Healthy coping includes planning, rest, exercise and talking with trusted people.
The learning self grows through self-regulated learning: setting goals, monitoring progress and adjusting strategies. SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.
Is "I will study more" a SMART goal?
A SMART version is "I will answer 30 practice questions every weekday for the next four weeks."
sections.answer: Not yet: it is not measurable or time-bound

lines: Erikson's stages continue into adulthood: identity versus role confusion in adolescence, intimacy versus isolation in young adulthood, then generativity versus stagnation in middle age.
When a question describes feeling energized before a challenge, think eustress; feeling unable to cope points to distress.
Thinking all stress is bad. Some stress improves focus and performance; the goal is to manage it, not remove it completely.

lessons.subject: The Teaching Profession
lessons.title: Philosophical and Social Foundations of Education

lines: Traditional philosophies: Idealism (ideas and character; the teacher as model), Realism (the physical world, observation and science), Perennialism (lasting truths and the "great books") and Essentialism (a core of basic knowledge and skills, teacher-led).

Learner-centered philosophies: Progressivism and Pragmatism (Dewey: learning by doing, education as life), Existentialism (personal choice and responsibility) and Social Reconstructionism (schools should lead social change).
A school stresses mastery of reading, writing, arithmetic and discipline, with the teacher directing learning. Which philosophy is this?
A common core of essential skills, taught systematically by the teacher, marks essentialism.

Sociological views: Functionalism (schools keep society stable by passing on shared values), Conflict theory (schools can reproduce inequality) and Symbolic interactionism (everyday interactions and labels shape learners' self-image).

Teacher expectations matter: the Pygmalion effect describes how high expectations can raise performance. Paulo Freire criticized "banking" education, in which teachers deposit facts into passive learners, and proposed dialogue instead.
Ask "Who is at the center?" Teacher and content point to idealism, realism, perennialism or essentialism; the learner points to progressivism or existentialism; society points to reconstructionism.
Confusing perennialism and essentialism. Both are content-centered, but perennialism focuses on timeless ideas and classics, while essentialism focuses on basic practical skills.

lessons.subject: The Teaching Profession
lessons.title: The Professional Teacher: Laws, Ethics and Standards

lines: Key laws: RA 7836 (Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act of 1994, which created the LET), RA 4670 (Magna Carta for Public School Teachers; actual classroom teaching of not more than six hours a day), RA 10912 (Continuing Professional Development), RA 10533 (K to 12) and RA 7610 (special protection of children).

The Board for Professional Teachers under the PRC conducts the examination; passers receive a certificate of registration and a professional license. Under RA 9293, which amended RA 7836, non-education graduates may take the secondary LET after earning at least 18 units of professional education.

The Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers requires fairness and impartiality, bars accepting gifts or favors in exchange for concessions, and bars deducting grades as punishment for misbehavior. Teachers are expected to live with honor and dignity and serve the community. Accepting a personal benefit, such as free seminars, for requiring learners to buy certain materials is a conflict of interest.

DepEd's Child Protection Policy (DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2012) protects learners from abuse, violence, exploitation and bullying. A teacher who learns of possible abuse reports it promptly to the school head or child protection committee, even if the child asks for secrecy, and does not investigate alone. Related laws: RA 10627 (Anti-Bullying Act of 2013) requires every school to adopt and carry out an anti-bullying policy, and RA 11596 (2021) prohibits child marriage, where either party is below 18.
How many domains does the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST) have?

The PPST (DepEd Order No. 42, s. 2017) has 7 domains and 37 strands, with four career stages: Beginning, Proficient, Highly Proficient and Distinguished. Proficient teachers work independently; Highly Proficient teachers consistently perform at a high level and mentor colleagues; Distinguished teachers are recognized leaders who embody the highest standard.

PPST domains: 1 Content Knowledge and Pedagogy, 2 Learning Environment, 3 Diversity of Learners, 4 Curriculum and Planning, 5 Assessment and Reporting, 6 Community Linkages and Professional Engagement, 7 Personal Growth and Professional Development.
Pair each law number with a keyword: 7836 license, 4670 welfare, 10912 CPD, 10533 K to 12, 7610 child protection.
Thinking a diploma alone allows a person to practice teaching. A professional license from the PRC is required.

lessons.subject: The Teaching Profession
lessons.title: The Philippine Education System and Inclusive Education

lines: The 1987 Constitution (Article XIV) gives education the highest budgetary priority, makes public elementary and high school education free, and guarantees academic freedom in institutions of higher learning. It also allows religion to be taught in public elementary and high schools within class hours, at the parents' written option, by instructors their church approves, at no cost to the government; and it requires schools, except those of religious groups and mission boards, to be at least 60% Filipino-owned.
Under the trifocal system (1994), DepEd manages basic education, CHED higher education (RA 7722) and TESDA technical-vocational education (RA 7796).

History: the American government set up public schools through Act No. 74 (1901), brought the Thomasites, and founded the Philippine Normal School (now Philippine Normal University) to train teachers.

Inclusive education places learners with disabilities in regular classes with support; RA 11650 (2022) institutionalizes it. An Individualized Education Plan (IEP) sets each learner's goals and services. Gifted learners need enrichment and acceleration. An accommodation changes how a learner learns or is assessed (written instructions, front seating, extra time) but keeps the same standards; a modification changes what is expected (fewer or simpler competencies).
A 20-year-old who left school in Grade 8 wants to finish basic education while working. Which DepEd program fits?
ALS serves out-of-school youth and adults outside the formal school system; RA 11510 (2020) institutionalized it.
Inclusion means bringing support to the learner in the regular class, not moving the learner to a separate room.

Assuming free public education under the Constitution covers college. Article XIV makes public elementary and high school free; free tuition in state universities comes from a separate law (RA 10931).

Glatthorn's types: recommended (by experts), written (the documented plan), taught, supported (resources and time), assessed and learned. The hidden curriculum is what learners pick up from school life; the null curriculum is what is left out.

Models: Tyler (start with objectives, then learning experiences, organization and evaluation) and Taba (grassroots: teachers design from their own classes). Backward design (Wiggins and McTighe) starts with desired results. Its three stages: identify desired results, determine acceptable evidence, then plan learning experiences. Taba's steps begin with teachers producing and testing pilot units.

Design ideas: scope (breadth and depth), sequence (order), vertical articulation (across grade levels), horizontal articulation (across subjects in a grade), and constructive alignment (outcomes, teaching and assessment match). Curriculum mapping charts what is taught, when and how it is assessed across grades and subjects, so that gaps and overlaps show up.
Curriculum foundations are its philosophical, psychological, social and historical bases.
Teachers lay out what each grade covers and find that fractions appear in Grades 3, 4 and 5, but percent is never taught. Which practice revealed this?
Curriculum mapping charts what is taught where, showing gaps (percent) and overlaps (fractions).
"Written" is the plan on paper; "taught" is what actually happens in class; "learned" is what learners actually gain. The three are often different.
Confusing the hidden and null curriculum. Hidden is learned without being planned; null is not taught at all.

lessons.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
lessons.title: Curriculum Development, Evaluation and K to 12

lines: Curriculum development moves through planning, designing, implementing and evaluating.

Evaluation can be formative (during development, to improve) or summative (after, to judge). Stufflebeam's CIPP model evaluates Context, Input, Process and Product. Context looks at needs, Input at plans and resources, Process at how the program is carried out, and Product at its results.
In K to 12, learners study fractions in Grade 3 and meet them again, more deeply, in Grade 5. Which feature is this?
Spiral progression revisits topics with increasing depth. K to 12 also stresses contextualization: linking lessons to learners' local setting.

RA 10533 (2013) set up K to 12: Kindergarten, six years of elementary, four years of Junior High (Grades 7 to 10) and two years of Senior High (Grades 11 and 12). The MELCs (2020) trimmed competencies for pandemic learning.
CIPP in order: Context (needs) comes before Input (plans and resources), Process (how it is carried out) and Product (results).
Thinking formative evaluation comes only after a program ends. Formative evaluation happens during development or implementation, to improve it; summative evaluation comes after, to judge it.

The MATATAG Curriculum is DepEd's revised K to 10 curriculum, launched on August 10, 2023. Its name comes from the MATATAG agenda, "Bansang Makabata, Batang Makabansa": MAke the curriculum relevant; TAke steps to accelerate delivery of basic education facilities and services; TAke good care of learners; Give support to teachers to teach better.

DepEd Order No. 010, s. 2024 (July 23, 2024) sets its implementation: Kindergarten to Grade 10 in three key stages (K to 3, Grades 4 to 6, Grades 7 to 10), phased in from SY 2024–2025 with Kindergarten and Grades 1, 4 and 7, and the other grade levels in the following school years (DepEd's July 2024 FAQ targets full implementation by SY 2026–2027). Senior High School keeps its current curriculum until a separate order, and grading still follows DO 8, s. 2015 until a new assessment policy is issued.

It answers a congested curriculum (in DepEd's review, typically fewer than 20% of teachers had time to teach all of a quarter's competencies) by reducing competencies, focusing on foundational literacy and numeracy, and embedding peace competencies. Grade 1 has five learning areas instead of seven: Language, Reading and Literacy, Mathematics, Makabansa, and GMRC. Makabansa (Grades 1 to 3) is transdisciplinary, covering civics, history, art and culture, and health and wellness. Mother Tongue is no longer a separate learning area; the language used for teaching in the early grades is a separate rule, which RA 12027 (2024) later changed.
In SY 2024–2025, a Grade 2 teacher asks whether her class may switch to the MATATAG Curriculum early. What does DO No. 010, s. 2024 say?
No. The phased implementation is the guide: a grade level follows the MATATAG Curriculum only from its own rollout year, and Grade 2 was not in the first group (Kindergarten and Grades 1, 4 and 7).
sections.answer: Not yet; each grade follows its rollout year

lines: MATATAG = MAke, TAke, TAke, Give: the curriculum, facilities and services, learners, and teachers.
Treating the MELCs as a new curriculum. They trimmed the existing K to 12 competencies for pandemic learning; the MATATAG Curriculum is the revised curriculum.

lessons.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
lessons.title: Objectives, Levels of Thinking and Lesson Planning

lines: A good objective is specific and measurable, naming an observable behavior, a condition and a standard: "Given a map, learners will locate five provinces with 100% accuracy." Avoid vague verbs such as understand, know and appreciate. The ABCD format names the Audience, Behavior, Condition ("given a ruler") and Degree ("with no errors").
Domains: cognitive (knowledge), affective (attitudes and values; Krathwohl: receiving, responding, valuing, organization, characterization) and psychomotor (skills).
Revised Bloom's taxonomy, lowest to highest: Remembering, Understanding, Applying, Analyzing, Evaluating, Creating.
"Which of the two proposed school rules is fairer? Defend your answer." At which level is this task?
Judging and defending a choice against criteria is evaluating.

Lesson formats: the 4A's (Activity, Analysis, Abstraction, Application), the 5E model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) and Herbart's steps (preparation, presentation, association, generalization, application). Gagné's Nine Events begin with gaining attention.
Ausubel's advance organizers link new material to what learners already know, supporting meaningful learning.
Match the verb to the level: list or define (remember), explain (understand), solve (apply), compare (analyze), judge (evaluate), design (create).
Writing "Learners will understand photosynthesis" as an objective. It cannot be measured; use "explain", "label" or "describe" instead.

lessons.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
lessons.title: Teaching Methods, Strategies and Classroom Management

lines: Deductive teaching states the rule first, then examples; inductive teaching goes from examples to the rule. Discovery and inquiry let learners find ideas with guidance. Project-based learning produces a product over time; problem-based learning starts with a messy real problem.

Cooperative learning (Johnson and Johnson) needs positive interdependence and individual accountability. Strategies include jigsaw, think-pair-share and peer tutoring. In STAD (Slavin), teams study together, members take quizzes alone, and the team earns points from each member's improvement. The Socratic method uses questions to expose contradictions in a learner's own reasoning.

Questioning: allow wait time (3 to 5 seconds); mix convergent (one answer) and divergent (many answers) questions; ask "why" to push higher-order thinking. Exit tickets give quick evidence of learning.

Classroom management: set rules and routines early; Kounin's withitness (knowing what is going on), overlapping (handling two things at once) and the ripple effect; the Canters' assertive discipline; Dreikurs's mistaken goals (attention, power, revenge).
Each member of a group becomes an expert on one part of a topic and teaches it to the rest. Which cooperative strategy is this?
In jigsaw, the group needs every member's part to complete the whole.

Inclusive and diverse classrooms: Universal Design for Learning plans multiple ways to engage, present and express from the start; multicultural education values all cultures; DepEd's IPEd makes education responsive to indigenous communities; multigrade teachers handle several grades in one room.
Graphic organizers make thinking visible: a concept map links ideas with labeled connections; a Venn diagram compares; a fishbone diagram shows causes and effects; a timeline shows sequence.
Intrinsic motivation grows from choice, relevance and a sense of progress; rewards and threats build only extrinsic motivation.
Calling any group work "cooperative learning". Without positive interdependence and individual accountability, one member may do all the work.

Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience runs from direct, purposeful experiences at the base (most concrete) to verbal symbols at the tip (most abstract). Realia (real objects), field trips and demonstrations sit near the base. The full order, from concrete to abstract: direct purposeful, contrived, dramatized experiences, demonstrations, study trips, exhibits, television, motion pictures, recordings and still pictures, visual symbols, verbal symbols.

Choose materials that match the objectives and the learners. Planning models: ASSURE (Analyze learners, State objectives, Select methods and materials, Utilize, Require participation, Evaluate and revise) and TPACK (technology, pedagogy and content knowledge working together).

SAMR describes levels of technology use: Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition. Modalities include blended learning, flipped classrooms, synchronous (live) and asynchronous (any time) online learning, and modular distance learning.
New literacies: media and information literacy, financial literacy, ecological literacy, digital citizenship and responsible use of AI tools.

Laws on technology in schools: RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012) protects personal information such as learners' names, grades and photos; RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code) covers copyright, so materials are credited and used lawfully; RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) penalizes offenses such as online libel and identity theft; and RA 10627 (Anti-Bullying Act of 2013) also covers cyberbullying.
A teacher posts learners' grades with their full names and home addresses in a public group chat. Which law does this most directly violate?
Learners' names, grades and addresses are personal information; sharing them publicly without consent violates the Data Privacy Act.
In the Cone of Experience, "doing" is at the bottom and "words" are at the top. The lower the level, the more concrete the experience.
Assuming newer technology is always better. Technology helps only when it fits the objective; a well-chosen chart can beat a flashy slide.

lessons.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
lessons.title: Theories of Development: Piaget, Vygotsky and Erikson

lines: Piaget's stages: sensorimotor (object permanence), preoperational (egocentrism, animism), concrete operational (conservation, reversibility) and formal operational (abstract and hypothetical thinking). Children actively construct knowledge through assimilation and accommodation. Preoperational children show centration, focusing on one feature (such as the length of a row) and ignoring others, which is why they fail conservation tasks.

Vygotsky: learning is social. The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and with help; scaffolding is support that is gradually removed; the more knowledgeable other guides; private speech helps children direct their thinking.

Erikson's crises: trust vs. mistrust (infancy), autonomy vs. shame, initiative vs. guilt (3 to 6), industry vs. inferiority (6 to 12), identity vs. role confusion (adolescence), intimacy vs. isolation (young adulthood).
A child knows that pouring juice into a taller glass does not change the amount. Which Piaget stage is this?
Understanding conservation marks the concrete operational stage, about ages 7 to 11.
Piaget asks "What can the child think?"; Vygotsky asks "What can the child do with help?"; Erikson asks "What crisis is the person facing?"
Mixing Erikson's adolescent stage (identity vs. role confusion) with the school-age stage (industry vs. inferiority).

lessons.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
lessons.title: Moral Development, Ecological Systems and Adolescence

lines: Kohlberg's moral levels: preconventional (stage 1 avoids punishment; stage 2 is instrumental exchange, "I'll help you if you help me"), conventional (stage 3 seeks approval; stage 4 keeps law and order) and postconventional (stage 5 sees rules as social agreements that can be changed for the common good; stage 6 follows universal ethical principles). Gilligan added an ethics of care.

Bronfenbrenner places the child within the microsystem (family, school), mesosystem (links between the microsystems), exosystem (settings that affect the child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace), macrosystem (culture and values) and chronosystem (changes over time, such as a family move or a parent's death).

Freud's psychosexual stages: oral (infancy), anal (about 1 to 3), phallic (about 3 to 6), latency (about 6 to puberty, when sexual interest is quiet and energy goes to school and friends) and genital (adolescence onward).

Adolescents go through a growth spurt and, in Elkind's terms, may believe in an imaginary audience (everyone is watching) and a personal fable (they are unique and invulnerable). Physical growth follows two directions: cephalocaudal (head to toe, so head control comes before walking) and proximodistal (center outward, so arm control comes before finger control).

Attachment (Bowlby; Ainsworth's Strange Situation): a securely attached child explores while the caregiver is near, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is quickly comforted on return; insecure patterns are avoidant, anxious-ambivalent (resistant) and disorganized. Secure attachment supports later confidence.

Marcia's identity statuses: diffusion (no exploration, no commitment), foreclosure (commitment without exploration, often to others' choices), moratorium (exploring, not yet committed) and achievement (commitment after exploration).
A toddler barely reacts when his mother leaves the room and ignores her when she comes back. Which attachment pattern does this suggest?
Avoiding the caregiver on return, with little distress at separation, marks avoidant attachment. A securely attached child is upset when the caregiver leaves and is quickly comforted on return.
Placing the family in the exosystem. The family is part of the child's microsystem; a parent's workplace, which the child is not part of, is the exosystem.
Behaviorism: classical conditioning (Pavlov, learning by association), operant conditioning (Skinner, behavior shaped by consequences) and Thorndike's laws of effect, exercise and readiness.

Reinforcement increases behavior (positive adds something pleasant; negative removes something unpleasant). Punishment decreases behavior. Extinction fades a behavior by removing its reinforcement; shaping rewards small steps toward a goal. The Premack principle uses a preferred activity to reward a less preferred one ("finish the worksheet, then read in the corner"). Schedules of reinforcement: fixed or variable ratio (after a number of responses) and fixed or variable interval (after time passes). Variable ratio gives high, steady responding that is slow to fade.
Learners who finish their work early are excused from cleaning duty, so more learners finish early. What is this?
Removing something unpleasant (cleaning) increases a behavior (finishing early). It is not punishment.

Bandura's social learning: we learn by observing models, through attention, retention, reproduction and motivation. Cognitive theories: insight learning (Köhler), latent learning (Tolman), Gestalt ("the whole is greater than its parts") and information processing (sensory memory, limited working memory, long-term memory; chunking helps). Working memory holds only about seven items (plus or minus two) at a time.

Humanistic psychology (Maslow, Rogers) centers on the whole person, self-worth and a caring climate. Metacognition is thinking about one's own thinking. Brain-based learning (Caine and Caine) applies findings about the brain: learners learn best in a safe, low-threat climate with "relaxed alertness", when lessons connect to their experiences and form meaningful patterns, and when practice is spaced over time rather than crammed. Emotion strongly affects attention and memory.
Negative reinforcement still increases behavior. If a behavior goes down, it is punishment or extinction.
Treating "negative" as "bad". In behaviorism, negative only means something is taken away.

lessons.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
lessons.title: Individual Differences, Motivation and Special Needs

lines: Gardner's multiple intelligences include linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalist. Sternberg's triarchic theory: analytical, creative and practical. Goleman popularized emotional intelligence.

Earlier views treat intelligence as one general ability: Spearman's g factor. Binet built the first practical intelligence test; the classic IQ is mental age ÷ chronological age × 100, so a 10-year-old with a mental age of 12 has an IQ of 120. Gardner and Sternberg later argued that intelligence has several distinct parts.
Differentiated instruction (Tomlinson) adjusts content, process, product and the learning environment to learners' readiness, interests and profiles.

Learning styles describe preferences: visual (pictures, diagrams), auditory (listening, discussion) and kinesthetic (movement, hands-on). Research does not show that matching lessons to one style improves learning, so present ideas in several modes instead of labeling learners.
Maslow: physiological needs come first, then safety, belonging, esteem and self-actualization. Intrinsic motivation comes from interest; extrinsic from rewards.

Bandura's self-efficacy is belief in one's ability to succeed at a task. It grows from mastery experiences (one's own successes, the strongest source), vicarious experiences (seeing similar others succeed), verbal persuasion and one's emotional and physical state. Learned helplessness is giving up after repeated failure; Dweck's growth mindset holds that ability grows with effort and good strategies. In Weiner's attribution theory, blaming failure on effort (internal, unstable, controllable) keeps learners trying; blaming low ability, luck or an unfair test does not. Social-emotional learning builds self-management, relationships and responsible decisions.
A learner keeps a journal of her goals and reflects on her feelings after each test. Which intelligence does this show?
Intrapersonal intelligence is self-knowledge; interpersonal intelligence is understanding others.

Special needs: dyslexia (reading and spelling), dyscalculia (mathematics), dysgraphia (handwriting and written expression), ADHD (inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity), autism (benefits from routines and visual schedules) and hearing impairment (sit near the front, facing the teacher).
In Maslow questions, first ask which lower need is unmet. A hungry or unsafe learner cannot focus on learning.
Mixing up interpersonal and intrapersonal. "Inter" is between people; "intra" is within oneself.

By timing and purpose: diagnostic (before instruction, to find gaps), formative (during, to guide teaching; assessment for learning), summative (after, to judge achievement; assessment of learning). Assessment as learning has learners monitor their own progress.

Norm-referenced tests compare learners with each other; criterion-referenced tests compare each learner with a standard. Authentic and performance assessment use real-life tasks; portfolios collect work over time to show growth.

Validity: the test measures what it should. Content validity (often ensured by a table of specifications), face validity (whether the test looks, on its surface, like it measures what it claims), and criterion validity such as predictive validity. Predictive validity compares scores with a criterion measured later (first-year grades); concurrent validity compares them with one measured at the same time.

Reliability: consistent results. Test-retest (same test twice), split-half (one test divided into two halves, adjusted with the Spearman-Brown formula) and internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha, KR-20), and inter-rater reliability (scorers agree). Other qualities: objectivity and practicality.
A science test is full of difficult English words, so learners who know the science still fail. Which quality is weakened most?
The test is measuring reading ability, not only science, so its validity suffers.

Assess each domain of learning with a fitting tool: cognitive (knowledge and thinking) with tests; affective (attitudes, values and interests) with checklists, rating scales and journals; psychomotor (physical skills) with performance tasks scored by rubrics.
Good feedback is specific, timely and tells the learner what to do next ("Add a source to support your second claim"), unlike vague comments ("Good job").
Reliability is consistency; validity is accuracy. A test can be reliable without being valid, but not valid without being reliable.
Calling every quiz "summative". A quiz used to adjust teaching is formative, whatever its format.

lessons.subject: Assessment of Learning
lessons.title: Test Construction, Item Analysis and Rubrics

lines: Selection-type items (multiple choice, true or false, matching) and supply-type items (completion, essay). Good multiple-choice options are plausible and similar in length; matching sets need more options than items; true-or-false items invite guessing.

Item analysis: the difficulty index is the proportion who answered correctly (about 0.50 separates learners best); the discrimination index compares high and low scorers. A negative index means low scorers did better, so revise or discard the item. In distractor analysis, a good wrong option attracts more low scorers than high scorers; one that attracts more high scorers may be ambiguous and needs revision.
Rubrics: holistic (one overall score) or analytic (a score per criterion), with descriptors for each level. Score essays with a rubric, without looking at names.
A teacher wants separate scores for the content, organization and grammar of learners' essays. Which kind of rubric fits?
An analytic rubric scores each criterion on its own, so learners see their strengths and weaknesses. A holistic rubric gives one overall score.
Difficulty asks "How many got it right?"; discrimination asks "Did the better learners get it right more often?"
Keeping an item just because most learners got it right. An item that almost everyone answers correctly tells the teacher very little about who has mastered the content.

Statistics: the mean is affected by extreme scores; the median is not; the mode is the most frequent score. Standard deviation shows spread. In a normal curve about 68% of scores lie within 1 SD of the mean. Positive skew means most scores are low (a hard test); negative skew means most are high. A z-score is (score − mean) ÷ SD, and a T-score is 50 + 10z, so T-scores have a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. Compare a learner's results in two subjects with z-scores, not raw scores.
A learner's z-score is +1. What does this mean?
A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean. +1 is above average, around the 84th percentile.
sections.answer: One standard deviation above the mean

lines: A percentile rank of 80 means scoring higher than 80% of the group, not getting 80% correct. Under DepEd Order No. 8, s. 2015, grades combine written work, performance tasks and quarterly assessment, with weights that depend on the subject. For Grades 1 to 10: Languages, Araling Panlipunan and EsP 30% / 50% / 20%; Science and Mathematics 40% / 40% / 20%; MAPEH and EPP/TLE 20% / 60% / 20%. The weighted initial grade is converted with a transmutation table, and 75 is the passing grade. Senior High School uses the same three components with its own weights, which depend on the track and the type of subject. Grading on a curve (norm-referenced grading) gives a fixed share of learners each grade; criterion-referenced grading compares each learner with set standards.
For skew, look at where the tail points: a tail toward high scores is positive skew; a tail toward low scores is negative skew.
Reading a percentile rank as a percentage score. They answer different questions: "better than how many?" versus "how many correct?"

Field study courses let pre-service teachers observe and take part in real classrooms through learning episodes: observe, analyze, reflect and document one aspect of teaching. Observation tools include anecdotal records (brief factual accounts), event recording (counting a behavior), checklists and rating scales.
Observers are guests: they coordinate with the school, keep learners' information confidential, take objective notes and never post learners' photos online.

Teaching internship progresses from observing and assisting, to teaching parts of lessons, to full classes, ending with a final demonstration. The cooperating teacher mentors and gives feedback; the college supervisor monitors and evaluates with the cooperating teacher.

Microteaching is a short lesson to peers focused on one skill; its cycle is plan, teach, get feedback, replan, reteach and get feedback again. A teaching portfolio holds lesson plans, learner work, observations and reflections.
Halfway through a lesson, an intern notices confused faces and switches to a concrete example. Which idea of Schön does this show?

Reflection-in-action happens during teaching; reflection-on-action happens afterward. Gibbs' cycle ends with an action plan. Its stages: description, feelings, evaluation (what was good and bad), analysis (why), conclusion and action plan.

Professionalism means punctuality, proper dress, keeping commitments, accepting feedback and keeping relationships with learners professional. School Learning Action Cells (LACs) let teachers learn together.

A good learning environment is physically safe and orderly (seating, lighting, displays of learners' work) and psychologically safe: rules made with the learners, respect for every learner, and no shaming. Professional boundaries: talk with learners through official school channels, not private chats; avoid favoritism, gifts and dating; and keep learners' personal information confidential.
When an observation question asks for "objective" notes, choose the option that describes what happened, not what the observer thinks of it.
Correcting the cooperating teacher in front of the class. Disagreements are raised privately and respectfully.

lessons.subject: Field Study and Action Research
